name: Hazel
description: Hazel is a Mac file-automation utility that watches selected folders and applies user-defined conditions and actions to their contents. It can organize, rename, tag, archive, upload, and remove files, manage Trash, clean up deleted applications, and extend workflows with macOS automation and scripts.
agentUseSummary: Hazel cannot yet be connected to Relay agents because its rules execute against local Mac files with broad folder, Trash, Full Disk Access, scripting, command, and upload authority, while Relay Marketplace does not currently ship a bounded device-local Hazel runtime or a supported remote Hazel API.

blocked.label: Connect Hazel
blocked.description: Relay does not present a Hazel license, installed-app state, monitored folder, macOS file permission, Full Disk Access grant, or local rules database as a Railway API connection.

blocked.label: Access Mac files
blocked.description: Relay does not inspect local paths, filenames, contents, metadata, Spotlight attributes, Trash, application support files, rule state, or synced rule files through an undisclosed device authority.

blocked.label: Run rules or scripts
blocked.description: Relay does not create, import, edit, enable, sync, or run Hazel rules or execute arbitrary AppleScript, JavaScript, Shortcuts, Automator workflows, shell scripts, command-line programs, or uploaded rule files.

blocked.label: Change or transmit files
blocked.description: Moving, copying, renaming, replacing, archiving, opening, tagging, importing, uploading, trashing, deleting, synchronizing, or otherwise changing or transmitting files remains unavailable until Relay ships explicit local authority and bounded approvals.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No agent actions can be enabled until Relay ships a separately disclosed, user-authorized Mac-local Hazel connector with strict path and action boundaries and no arbitrary-code surface.

runtimeSupport.description: Relay does not silently bridge OpenClaw to Hazel's local folder monitors, rules, Full Disk Access, scripts, commands, uploads, or Trash authority.
Relay does not silently bridge Hermes to Hazel's local folder monitors, rules, Full Disk Access, scripts, commands, uploads, or Trash authority.

providerSetup.blocker: Hazel is an installed Mac application whose rules monitor user-selected folders and can read file content and metadata; move, replace, upload, trash, or delete files; clean application support files; and run arbitrary AppleScript, JavaScript, Shortcuts, Automator workflows, shell scripts, or command-line programs. Trash features can require macOS Full Disk Access. Rule synchronization writes the complete ruleset to a user-selected external file rather than providing a hosted Hazel service. The reviewed first-party materials do not document a remote API, OAuth contract, webhook contract, developer console, or remote MCP service, and Relay's current Marketplace runtime excludes local-app and filesystem command execution.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request Hazel license files or macOS permissions; inspect folders, rules, logs, Trash, support files, or synchronized rule files; import rules; execute scripts or commands; automate the app UI; or show Connect. Reconsider only after Relay ships a disclosed Mac-local connector with verified app presence, explicit per-folder grants, canonical path enforcement, symlink and traversal defenses, typed non-arbitrary actions, previews, mutation and upload approvals, bounded results, redaction, audit, revocation, and no Railway fallback.

evidence.supports: Noodlesoft describes Hazel as Mac automation that watches selected folders, organizes files with rules, manages Trash and application leftovers, and integrates with Shortcuts, AppleScript, and Automator.
Hazel's official guide documents local folder monitoring, automatic file actions, selective Trash deletion, and App Sweep cleanup of application support files.
Hazel rules can examine file contents and metadata and can move, copy, rename, upload, trash, tag, import, or open files and run AppleScript, JavaScript, Automator, Shortcuts, and shell scripts.
Hazel's action reference documents destructive replacement and deletion behavior, FTP/SFTP/WebDAV uploads, arbitrary command-line execution, recursive rule processing, and local automation actions.
Noodlesoft documents macOS folder-access prompts and a Full Disk Access requirement for Hazel's Trash-related features.
Hazel rule sync uses a user-selected external file in locations such as iCloud Drive, Dropbox, or a network server and can overwrite a complete local folder ruleset; it is not a hosted Hazel API.
